problem.title: Ribbon Length
problem.statement: A ribbon has a plain section 4 cm long followed by k colored sections, each 5 cm long. Which expression gives the total length in centimeters?
hints: Name the quantity that the letter counts, then follow the operations in the story.

solutionSteps.title: Translate and check
solutionSteps.body: Each of the k colored sections contributes 5 cm, for 5k cm. Add the one plain section: 4 + 5k.

validationMethods: Direct semantic translation: Each of the k colored sections contributes 5 cm, for 5k cm. Add the one plain section: 4 + 5k.
Independent concrete-case and option audit: At k = 0 only 4 cm remains; at k = 2, direct concatenation gives 4 + 5 + 5 = 14 cm. Only choice A passes both checks.
notes: Only whole-number arithmetic and reading relationships are required; no equation-solving algorithm is assumed.

problem.title: One Letter, Several Inputs
problem.statement: Let t be the number of pages read after breakfast. Before breakfast Jo read 6 pages. Which statement correctly describes 6 + t?

choices.label: A
choices.text: t means a page, not a number

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an equation with answer 6

choices.label: D
choices.text: It gives 8 when t = 2 and 11 when t = 5

problem.shortAnswer: It gives 8 when t = 2 and 11 when t = 5
hints: Name the quantity that the letter counts, then follow the operations in the story.

solutionSteps.title: Translate and check
solutionSteps.body: t counts pages read after breakfast. Add it to the six earlier pages. Substitution gives 6 + 2 = 8 and 6 + 5 = 11.

validationMethods: Direct semantic translation: t counts pages read after breakfast. Add it to the six earlier pages. Substitution gives 6 + 2 = 8 and 6 + 5 = 11.

Independent concrete-case and option audit: Count six earlier pages plus two later pages, then six earlier plus five later: totals eight and eleven. Review each other statement against those two concrete cases.
notes: Only whole-number arithmetic and reading relationships are required; no equation-solving algorithm is assumed.

problem.title: Empty Seats
problem.statement: A room has 30 chairs. There are g groups of 4 students, with every student in exactly one group and every student seated in a different chair. Which equation states that exactly 6 chairs are empty?
hints: Name the quantity that the letter counts, then follow the operations in the story.

solutionSteps.title: Translate and check
solutionSteps.body: The groups occupy 4g chairs, so 30 − 4g chairs are empty. Equating this expression to six gives 30 − 4g = 6.

validationMethods: Direct semantic translation: The groups occupy 4g chairs, so 30 − 4g chairs are empty. Equating this expression to six gives 30 − 4g = 6.

Independent concrete-case and option audit: Six empty chairs leave 24 occupied chairs, which form six groups of four. At g = 6 only choice B is true; its left side also matches the occupied/empty partition.
notes: Only whole-number arithmetic and reading relationships are required; no equation-solving algorithm is assumed.

problem.title: A Claim Can Be False
problem.statement: Let q = 3. Which card is an equation whose equality claim is false?
hints: Name the quantity that the letter counts, then follow the operations in the story.

solutionSteps.title: Translate and check
solutionSteps.body: The cards with an equals sign are equations. With q = 3, 5 + q is 8, so 5 + q = 9 is false. The other equations say 8 = 8 and 9 = 9.

validationMethods: Direct semantic translation: The cards with an equals sign are equations. With q = 3, 5 + q is 8, so 5 + q = 9 is false. The other equations say 8 = 8 and 9 = 9.
Independent concrete-case and option audit: Evaluate equality cards separately: B compares 8 with 8; C compares 8 with 9; D compares 9 with 9. Cards A and E have no equality claim.
notes: Only whole-number arithmetic and reading relationships are required; no equation-solving algorithm is assumed.

problem.title: Pack Then Set Aside
problem.statement: Each of b boxes contains 4 red counters and 2 blue counters. After all boxes are emptied, 3 counters are set aside. Which equation says that 27 counters remain?
hints: Name the quantity that the letter counts, then follow the operations in the story.

solutionSteps.title: Translate and check
solutionSteps.body: Each box contains six counters, so all boxes contain 6b counters. Setting aside three once leaves 6b − 3. Either order of the two sides states that the remainder is 27.

validationMethods: Direct semantic translation: Each box contains six counters, so all boxes contain 6b counters. Setting aside three once leaves 6b − 3. Either order of the two sides states that the remainder is 27.

Independent concrete-case and option audit: Rebuild the situation: 27 remaining plus 3 set aside gives 30 counters, or five boxes of six. For b = 5 the choices compare 19, 33, 12, 11, and 27 with 27; only E matches. This also checks that subtraction happens once, after unpacking.
notes: Only whole-number arithmetic and reading relationships are required; no equation-solving algorithm is assumed.
